sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Anind is an Irish hero. He was one of the sons of the early invader Nemed. He is tied to a great feature of the Irish land, Lough Ennell in County Westmeath. That part of Ireland had no water on the surface. Men dug Anind’s grave, and the lake flooded forth at once. Tales of how a landscape formed often point to an old god with the power to create.

okr.objective: Record Anind, an Irish hero and son of Nemed.
